headline: Registration for Labrador's Vast Wilderness Preserve
reservation: Visitors must register with Parks Canada prior to entering this remote reserve to ensure safety monitoring in the subarctic backcountry. This administrative registration is distinct from booking local boat or floatplane charters, which are handled by private operators. Current access protocols and potential area closures should be verified directly through the Parks Canada Labrador office.

days.title: Boreal Forests and Cultural Heritage
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Happy Valley-Goose Bay

stops.name: Wonderstrands
stops.detail: Walk the historic 50-kilometre stretch of sandy beach mentioned in Viking sagas, observing the transition from tide to tundra.

stops.name: North West River
stops.detail: Visit the gateway community to understand the Innu and Inuit cultural significance of the Akami-Uapishkᵁ landscape.

days.driving: Allow for multi-hour boat transfers or air charters; conditions vary significantly by weather.
days.note: Marine travel is subject to high winds and tide cycles in Lake Melville.

days.title: Subarctic Tundra and High Peaks

stops.name: Mealy Mountains Plateau
stops.detail: Explore the alpine tundra where the resident Mealy Mountains caribou herd is known to roam.

stops.name: Uapishkᵁ Summits
stops.detail: Navigate the ancient rock formations of the 'white mountains' for panoramic views of the Labrador interior.

days.driving: Internal travel is strictly by foot or guided excursion; no developed roads exist within the park.
days.note: Black flies and mosquitoes are prevalent; peak activity varies by seasonal temperature.

days.title: Coastal Labrador Vistas

stops.name: Cape Porcupine
stops.detail: Observe the dramatic headlands where the Mealy Mountains meet the Atlantic Ocean.

stops.name: Pack's Harbour
stops.detail: View the coastal islands that form the eastern maritime boundary of the national park reserve.

days.driving: Allow a full day for water-based transit back to regional hubs; conditions vary.
days.note: Icebergs may be present in the offshore waters during the early summer season.

intel.title: Charter Requirements
intel.text: Access is primarily via floatplane from Goose Bay or boat from North West River and Cartwright. Travelers must coordinate with licensed outfitters as there is no road access into the park core.

intel.title: Communication Gaps
intel.text: Cellular service ends at the gateway town limits. Satellite communication devices are the only reliable method for emergency contact within the Mealy Mountains.

intel.title: Supply Management
intel.text: Final fuel and food supplies must be secured in Happy Valley-Goose Bay. There are no commercial services, stores, or fuel stations within the park boundaries.

intel.title: Seasonal Window
intel.text: The primary visiting window is mid-July to early September when snow has cleared the plateau. Earlier attempts often face impassable ice or significant snowpack in the high country.

intel.title: Gateway Staging
intel.text: Vehicle parking is limited to designated municipal lots in North West River or long-term airport parking in Goose Bay. Ensure your vehicle is secured before departing on multi-day charters.

plan.arrival: Upon landing at YYR, collect rental vehicle for town transit, purchase all bear-safety canisters and dehydrated supplies in Happy Valley-Goose Bay, and check in at the Parks Canada office.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are sufficient for gateway towns, but high-clearance 4WD is recommended for gravel roads near Cartwright; verify rental insurance for unpaved surfaces.
plan.goldenHour: Wonderstrands during the late summer sunset, though lighting varies with coastal fog patterns.
